original_value: Understanding the roles of social factors in online purchase behavior has been a long standing research problem. The recently emerging social e-commerce platforms leverage the stimulated word-of-mouth effect to promote the sales of items, which offers a peek into the complex interplay between the social influence and online purchasing behavior. In this paper, we investigate this problem on a full-scale purchase behavior dataset from one of the leading social e-commerce platforms, Beidian. Specifically, we conduct a comparison study between the social e-commerce and conventional e-commerce that are both integrated in Beidian to examine how social factors affect user's purchase behavior. We reveal that social e-commerce leads to a 3.09~10.37 times higher purchase conversion rate compared with the conventional settings, which indicates users make purchase with significantly fewer item explorations. Then, we propose and validate four primary mechanisms that contribute to the efficient purchase conversion: better matching, social enrichment, social proof and price sensitivity. Moreover, we identify several behavioral indicators that are able to measure the effect of these mechanisms, based on which we design an accurate predictive model (AUC=0.7738) for user's purchase decision. These results combine to shed light on how to understand and model the purchase behavior in social e-commerce.

result.paraphrase: Understanding how social factors shape online purchase behavior has long been a research challenge. Emerging social e-commerce platforms harness word-of-mouth effects to boost item sales, providing insight into the complex interaction between social influence and online buying. In this paper, we examine the issue using a full-scale purchase behavior dataset from Beidian, one of the leading social e-commerce platforms. Specifically, we compare the social e-commerce and conventional e-commerce functions integrated in Beidian to study how social factors influence users' purchase behavior. We find that social e-commerce produces a purchase conversion rate 3.09 to 10.37 times higher than conventional settings, meaning users buy after significantly fewer item explorations. We then propose and validate four main mechanisms behind the efficient conversion: better matching, social enrichment, social proof, and price sensitivity. In addition, we identify several behavioral indicators that can measure these mechanisms, and based on them we build an accurate predictive model for users' purchase decisions (AUC=0.7738). Together, these findings help explain and model purchase behavior in social e-commerce.
